title: Stanford CS329Z | Engineering AI Agents

CS 329Z: Engineering AI Agents

Stanford / Fall 2026

Instructors

Diyi Yang, Instructor

Michael Ryan, Instructor

John Yang, Instructor

Owen Queen, TA

Anusheh Chaudry, TA

Shreyas Sharma, TA

Houjun Liu, TA

Welcome!

The shift from monolithic language models to compound AI systems — systems with multiple interacting components including LLMs, retrievers, tools, and optimizers — represents a fundamental change in how AI applications are built for people. This course teaches students how to engineer agentic systems: the full spectrum from simple LLM pipelines to compound AI systems to autonomous agents. Students will learn to pick what types of problems to focus on, decompose problems, select appropriate components, collect and curate data, build evaluations, and reason about the design tradeoffs that arise when building these systems in practice.

Students first build core components (RAG, tool use, agent loops) from scratch, then learn how frameworks like DSPy abstract these patterns. Through two fully applied homework assignments and a quarter-long project, students gain hands-on experience building, optimizing, and evaluating agentic systems.

For more information about coursework, office hours, and logistics, please refer to the Logistics page. You can also view course dates on the Google Calendar.

Class Schedule

Note: the schedule is tentative and subject to change. Classes meet Mondays and Wednesdays, 1:30–2:50 p.m., in Skilling Auditorium. Lecture materials will be linked here as they are released.

WeekDateLectureCourse Material
1Wed Sep 23Foundations & Landscape Introduction — What Are Agentic Systems? A brief history of agents; the anatomy of an agent (LLM core, reasoning, memory, tools, environment); compound AI systems and workflows vs. agents; key challenges in reliability, training, safety, and evaluation; course logistics.Readings:
2Mon Sep 28LLMs for Builders Language model internals for agent builders: decoding strategies, transformer attention (including linear and hybrid) and context length, the pretraining-to-post-training pipeline, inference and test-time scaling, structured I/O and constrained decoding, and context engineering.Readings:
2Wed Sep 30Building Blocks Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Why retrieval; indexing (chunking, contextual retrieval, RAPTOR, HNSW); retrievers from BM25 and DPR to hybrid search, reranking, and ColBERT; agentic RAG (Self-RAG, Search-R1); RAG failure modes. Plus a course project overview.Readings:
3Mon Oct 5Tool Use & Function Calling Why LLMs need tools; learning to call tools (Toolformer) and scaling to thousands of APIs (Gorilla, ToolLLM); standard interfaces from REST to function calling to MCP; evaluating tool use (BFCL, ToolBench, τ-bench); failure modes.Readings:
3Wed Oct 7Frameworks & Agent Design Frameworks & Orchestration The data/system/evals pillars; live demos of DSPy (signatures, modules, optimizers) and LangGraph (state, nodes, edges); open-source agent harnesses (mini-SWE-agent, OpenHands, Pi); durable orchestration with Temporal and observability tooling; best practices.Readings:
4Mon Oct 12Agent Design Patterns & Scaffolds Workflows vs. agents; five composable workflow patterns; reasoning and acting patterns (ReAct, Reflexion, CodeAct, ReWOO); context-management patterns (event logs, compaction, observation masking, context isolation); case study of the Pi harness.Readings:
4Wed Oct 14Memory & Multi-Agent Systems Agent Memory Architectures Why agents need memory; working, episodic, semantic, and procedural memory; four architecture patterns (skill libraries, tiered hierarchies like MemGPT, reflective consolidation, memory maintenance); memory benchmarks; open problems in forgetting, privacy, and over-personalization.Readings:
5Mon Oct 19Multi-Agent Systems When to use single vs. multi-agent systems; orchestration patterns (orchestrator, swarm, hybrid); communication via handoffs, message boards, and the A2A protocol; coordination infrastructure (task ledgers, shared memory, worktree isolation); why multi-agent systems fail.Readings:
5Wed Oct 21Optimization Optimization The landscape from prompts to fine-tuning; prompt optimization (GEPA, MIPROv2, OPRO, TextGrad); test-time compute scaling; LoRA/QLoRA; distillation; RLHF/DPO at a high level; and when to optimize prompts vs. weights vs. inference compute.Readings:
6Mon Oct 26 📺 Guest Lecture: Terminal-Bench Ryan Marten, Alex Shaw Ryan Marten and Alex Shaw (Laude Institute), co-creators of Terminal-Bench, on benchmarking how well AI agents accomplish real-world tasks in a terminal environment. Readings:
6Wed Oct 28Data for Agentic Systems What Data Do Agents Need? Traces, demonstrations, and feedback; data for optimization vs. evaluation; data flywheels; synthetic data generation; collecting data from human-agent interaction.Readings:
7Mon Nov 2Data Selection & Quality Finding maximally informative data, filtering and selection strategies, tiny-but-targeted benchmarks, annotation practices, quality assessment, and building datasets from agent traces. Readings:

Additional readings
7Wed Nov 4Evaluation for Agentic Systems Evaluation Fundamentals & Benchmark Design Why evals are hard, the 4-tuple framework (request, environment, stopping criteria, scorer), designing each component, properties of good benchmarks, realistic scaffolding, and reliability dimensions.Readings:
8Mon Nov 9LLM-as-Judge & Evaluation Infrastructure The three grader types, designing judge prompts, known biases, pairwise vs. pointwise evaluation, non-determinism metrics (pass@k vs. pass^k), harness design, and Anthropic's 8-step roadmap.Readings:
8Wed Nov 11Safety Agent Safety & Guardrails Privacy risks of tool access, prompt injection (including indirect injection), red-teaming, sandboxing and permission models, output guardrails, liability considerations, responsible deployment, and human-in-the-loop patterns.Readings:
9Mon Nov 16📺 Guest Lecture (TBA)
9Wed Nov 18Coding Agents & Proactive Agents Coding & Software Agents How coding agents work end-to-end; SWE-agent, Claude Code, and OpenHands architectures; scaffolds as design decisions; SWE-bench and the 4-tuple framework in practice; the future of software development with agents.Readings:
10Mon Nov 23No Class — Thanksgiving Recess
10Wed Nov 25No Class — Thanksgiving Recess
11Mon Nov 30Proactive Agents From reactive to proactive; General User Models (GUM); Next Action Prediction; open-source proactive personal agents; privacy and trust implications; and when agents should initiate vs. wait (mixed initiative).Readings:
11Wed Dec 2Open Problems & Final Demos Frontiers & Open Problems Multimodal agents, web agents and computer use, science agents, long-running agent architectures, production and observability (tracing, monitoring, cost management), and open problems in reliability, scalability, and interpretability.
—Finals Week (Dec 7–11)Final Project Demo Day Held during the end-quarter examination period; exact time and location TBA.

summary_zh: Stanford CS329Z《Engineering AI Agents》是 2026 年秋季课程，由 Diyi Yang 等讲授，讲如何工程化构建从简单 LLM 流水线到复合 AI 系统再到自主 Agent 的全谱系系统。学生先从零实现 RAG、工具调用和 Agent 循环等核心组件，再学习 DSPy、LangGraph 等框架如何抽象这些模式。课程表覆盖面向开发者的 LLM 原理、RAG（混合检索、重排、Agentic RAG）、工具调用与 MCP 及其评测、框架与编排（含 OpenHands 等开源 harness、Temporal 持久化编排）、Agent 设计模式与上下文管理、记忆与多智能体系统等。课程包含两个应用型作业和一个学期项目，强调问题拆解、数据整理、构建评测和设计权衡。
title_zh: 斯坦福CS329Z |工程AI 智能体
html_zh:
CS 329Z：工程AI 智能体

斯坦福大学 / 2026 年秋季

导师

杨迪怡，讲师

迈克尔·瑞安，讲师

杨约翰，讲师

欧文·奎恩，助教

阿努谢·乔德里，TA

施里亚斯·夏尔马，是的

Houjun Liu, TA

欢迎！

从单一语言模型到复合人工智能系统（具有LLM、检索器、工具和优化器等多个交互组件的系统）的转变代表了为人们构建人工智能应用程序的方式发生了根本性变化。本课程教授学生如何设计代理系统：从简单的LLM管道到复合人工智能系统再到自主代理的全方位。学生将学习选择要关注的问题类型、分解问题、选择适当的组件、收集和整理数据、建立评估以及推理在实践中构建这些系统时出现的设计权衡。

学生首先从头开始构建核心组件（RAG、工具使用、代理循环），然后学习 DSPy 等框架如何抽象这些模式。通过两项完全应用的家庭作业和一个为期四分之一的项目，学生获得构建、优化和评估代理系统的实践经验。

有关课程作业、办公时间和后勤的更多信息，请参阅后勤页面。您还可以在Google 日历上查看课程日期。

课程表

注意：时间表是暂定的，可能会发生变化。课程每周一和周三下午 1:30–2:50 在 Skilling Auditorium 举行。讲座材料发布后将在此处链接。

星期日期演讲课程材料
19 月 23 日星期三基础和景观介绍——什么是代理系统？代理人简史；代理的剖析（LLM 核心、推理、内存、工具、环境）；复合人工智能系统和工作流程与代理；可靠性、培训、安全性和评估方面的关键挑战；课程物流。读物：
29 月 28 日星期一面向构建者的LLM 面向代理构建者的语言模型内部结构：解码策略、变换器注意力（包括线性和混合）和上下文长度、训练前到训练后管道、推理和测试时间缩放、结构化 I/O 和约束解码以及上下文工程。读物：
29 月 30 日星期三检索构建模块 - 增强生成 (RAG) 为什么检索；索引（分块、上下文检索、RAPTOR、HNSW）；检索器从 BM25 和 DPR 到混合搜索、重新排名和 ColBERT；代理 RAG（Self-RAG、Search-R1）； RAG 故障模式。加上课程项目概述。读物：
310 月 5 日星期一工具使用和函数调用 为什么LLM需要工具；学习调用工具 (Toolformer) 并扩展到数千个 API (Gorilla、ToolLLM)；从 REST 到 MCP 函数调用的标准接口；评估工具使用情况（BFCL、ToolBench、τ-bench）；失效模式。读物：
310 月 7 日星期三框架和代理设计框架和编排数据/系统/评估支柱； DSPy（签名、模块、优化器）和 LangGraph（状态、节点、边）的现场演示；开源代理工具（mini-SWE-agent、OpenHands、Pi）；使用时间和可观察性工具进行持久编排；最佳实践。读物：
410 月 12 日星期一代理设计模式和支架 工作流程与代理；五种可组合的工作流程模式；推理和行动模式（ReAct、Reflexion、CodeAct、ReWOO）；上下文管理模式（事件日志、压缩、观察屏蔽、上下文隔离）； Pi 线束的案例研究。读物：
410 月 14 日星期三内存和多智能体系统代理内存架构为什么代理需要内存；工作记忆、情景记忆、语义记忆和程序记忆；四种架构模式（技能库、MemGPT 等分层结构、反射整合、内存维护）；内存基准测试；遗忘、隐私和过度个性化等开放性问题。读物：
510 月 19 日星期一多智能体系统 何时使用单代理系统与多智能体系统；编排模式（编排模式、群体模式、混合模式）；通过切换、留言板和 A2A 协议进行通信；协调基础设施（任务分类账、共享内存、工作树隔离）；为什么多智能体系统会失败。读物：
510 月 21 日星期三优化 优化景观从提示到微调；提示优化（GEPA、MIPROv2、OPRO、TextGrad）；测试时计算缩放； LoRA/QLoRA；蒸馏；高水平的 RLHF/DPO；以及何时优化提示、权重和推理计算。读物：
610 月 26 日星期一📺 客座讲座：Terminal-Bench Ryan Marten 、 Alex Shaw Ryan Marten 和 Alex Shaw（Laude Institute）是 Terminal-Bench 的联合创始人，他们对AI 智能体在终端环境中完成现实世界任务的情况进行基准测试。 读物：
610 月 28 日星期三代理系统的数据 代理需要什么数据？痕迹、示范、反馈；用于优化与评估的数据；数据飞轮；合成数据生成；从人机交互中收集数据。读物：
711 月 2 日星期一数据选择和质量查找信息量最大的数据、过滤和选择策略、微小但有针对性的基准、注释实践、质量评估以及从代理跟踪构建数据集。读物：

附加读物
711 月 4 日星期三代理系统的评估 评估基础和基准设计 为什么评估很困难，四元组框架（请求、环境、停止标准、评分器）、设计每个组件、良好基准的属性、现实的脚手架和可靠性维度。读物：
811 月 9 日星期一LLM 作为法官和评估基础设施 三种评分者类型、设计法官提示、已知偏差、成对评估与逐点评估、非确定性指标（pass@k 与 pass^k）、工具设计和 Anthropic 的 8 步路线图。读物：
811 月 11 日星期三安全代理安全与护栏工具访问、提示注入（包括间接注入）、红队、沙箱和权限模型、输出护栏、责任考虑、负责任的部署和人机参与模式的隐私风险。读物：
911 月 16 日星期一📺 客座讲座（待定）
911 月 18 日星期三编码代理和主动代理 编码和软件代理 编码代理如何端到端工作； SWE-agent、Claude Code 和 OpenHands 架构；脚手架作为设计决策； SWE-bench 和四元组框架的实践；与代理商一起开发软件的未来。读物：
1011 月 23 日星期一没有课——感恩节课间休息
1011 月 25 日星期三没有课——感恩节课间休息
1111 月 30 日星期一主动代理从被动到主动；通用用户模型（GUM）；下一步行动预测；开源主动个人代理；隐私和信任影响；以及代理何时应发起与等待（混合主动）。读物：
1112 月 2 日星期三开放问题和最终演示 前沿和开放问题 多模式代理、网络代理和计算机使用、科学代理、长期运行的代理架构、生产和可观察性（跟踪、监控、成本管理）以及可靠性、可扩展性和可解释性方面的开放问题。
—决赛周（12 月 7 日至 11 日）最终项目演示日在季末考试期间举行；具体时间和地点待定。
